children: Australia's GDP growth held up respectably in the June quarter, but its composition doesn't point to a re-accelerating economy, says Sunny Nguyen, Head of Australia Economics at Moody's Analytics. Private investment fell, consumers saved rather than spent, and net trade was positive only because people stopped traveling, Nguyen says in an email. While Moody's base case still has the Reserve Bank of Australia holding rates in September, Nguyen sees risk of a November hike as significantly higher. If the September-quarter trimmed mean inflation is at or above 0.9% on quarter, RBA will have little choice but to move the needle again, she adds.(monica.gupta@wsj.com)
